robots.name: Pip — postal sorter
robots.design: A compact red enamel POST-BOX robot, waist high to a human: softly rounded rectangular body, domed postal-red lid, one large round amber face window in a brass rim, two tiny glowing oval spark-eyes and NO mouth/nose. Below it two simple pigeonhole cubbies hold envelopes; a routine card slot sits under the lid. Two small red mitten hands on short solid arms, one plain canvas satchel attached to its side. The entire body sits DIRECTLY on a small teal rolling chassis with two large rubber wheels and one hidden little caster. No legs, boots, walking struts or floating body. Distinct post-box silhouette, small readable forms. WORK: lift an envelope from a cubby and place it into the open satchel.

robots.name: Trowel — gardener
robots.design: A low rounded watering-can robot in soft mint/cream enamel, two-thirds of a person's height. One round brass-rimmed amber face with two glowing oval eyes, no mouth or nose; a plain spout arm with a perforated rose, a tiny opposite mitten grip, a small seed hopper at the back and just a few tidy leaves near its cap. Its body attaches directly to a broad two-wheel teal chassis with a little rear caster, no legs or feet. Oversized soft rubber wheels handle cobbles. Warm, contented domestic garden tool silhouette; not a human wearing robot clothes. WORK: tilt the spout and water a small potted seedling within the same cell, then return it upright.

robots.name: Wick — lamplighter
robots.design: A taller slim cream-enamel lamplighter, about adult shoulder height, with a small teal pagoda-like lantern cap, ONE brass-rimmed round amber face in the lantern head, two glowing eyes, no human face. Its narrow body mounts directly to a stable rounded cream/teal wheelbase with two FAT rubber wheels and a little caster; no long leg-like posts beneath the body. Short simple arms hold a telescoping brass lighting pole close to the body during rolling. The pole folds short enough to fit the frame. WORK: raise/extend the pole toward a small lamp fitting at the cell edge, touch it to light it, keeping all parts visible and mechanically connected.

robots.name: Heron — yard crane
robots.design: A friendly compact teal yard crane, wider and a little taller than a person. A rounded teal/cream body with ONE large round brass-rimmed amber spark-eye window sits directly on a broad FOUR-WHEEL rubber chassis, no legs or feet. A clean hinged teal boom with brass pivot discs rises from the back, a real cable runs over its tip to a rounded brass hook. Keep the boom compact/folded for travel, visually simple and cute rather than industrial gear clutter. Body, chassis, boom, pivots, cable and hook remain coherent across every view. WORK: smoothly lift one small wooden crate a little above the ground, then settle it down, no enormous crane swinging outside its cell.

robots.name: Tender — maintenance helper
robots.design: A squat tortoise-shaped cream-and-teal maintenance robot, knee high, with a broad soft dome shell, one large round brass-rimmed amber spark-face with two glowing oval eyes, and two short folding mitten arms curled beside its front. Four small rubber wheels tuck into a low teal chassis attached directly under the body. A small neat moss patch grows at the rear seam; otherwise cared for and friendly. A discreet routine slot and rear service hatch. No legs, insect appendages or scary exposed machinery. WORK: open a small inspection cover on a short pipe segment and gently turn a reachable valve with one mitten, then tuck the arm away.

robots.name: Tally — trading assistant
robots.design: A new small friendly merchant's assistant in cream enamel with muted ochre and deep teal accents, roughly waist high. Soft rounded-rectangle body like an old shop cashbox, one large circular brass-rimmed amber spark-face with two simple glowing oval eyes, no mouth/nose. A shallow securely attached counting tray at the front, a narrow receipt/routine slot, two stubby mitten arms, and a small till drawer low in the body. The body mounts DIRECTLY on two broad rubber wheels and a small rear caster. A few large simple coin discs, no written prices or currency branding. WORK: count/place one coin onto the tray, offer a short receipt, then return to the neutral travelling pose. Simple charming municipal machine, not a humanoid bank clerk.
